[How the collaboration works]{.eyebrow}

The 2026 AIM workshop used eight working groups to develop the research agenda. The ongoing collaboration consolidates that work into six connected research streams so that each project has a clear mathematical question, biological interpretation, data pathway, and practical audience.

| Research stream | Core work | Near-term output |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline colony dynamics | Reference model and modular stressor extensions | Technical report and reproducible implementation |
| Multi-stressor resilience | Bifurcations, multiple attractors, thresholds | Stressor-interaction and resilience analyses |
| Early warning analytics | Sensor time series and colony records | Pilot study and validated warning candidates |
| Intervention optimisation | Treatment, feeding, splitting, overwintering | Testable decision rules and optimisation paper |
| Climate–landscape integration | Weather, forage, spatial exposure | Climate sensitivity and landscape-linked models |
| Hybrid mechanistic–AI | State estimation and data assimilation | Reusable modelling and uncertainty pipeline |

## Cross-cutting responsibilities

Each stream shares four responsibilities:

1. **Biological grounding.** State the mechanism, scale, and assumptions with field and laboratory partners.
2. **Data stewardship.** Record variable definitions, temporal resolution, provenance, access constraints, and missingness in the shared crosswalk.
3. **Mathematical validation.** Separate structural conclusions from parameter-dependent results and report uncertainty.
4. **Translation.** Define the management or research decision the output is intended to improve.

## Coordination rhythm

Sub-teams work on focused milestones, with cross-stream sessions used to reconcile shared variables, compare model structures, and review results that affect more than one project. Code, documentation, and public outputs are linked through the [data and software](../data.qmd) page.

::: {.panel}
[Participation]{.eyebrow}

Contributors may join a research stream for a specific dataset, method, or field question; participation does not require involvement in every activity. Current workshop participants and areas of expertise are listed on the [People](../people.qmd) page.
:::

The [roadmap](../roadmap.qmd) provides the shared phases and deliverables. Questions suitable for new collaborations are collected under [open problems](open-problems.qmd).
